title: The lease renewal
scenario:
You manage the office of a 25-person design studio. The landlord sends an 18-page lease renewal and wants it signed within a week. You ask the studio's approved AI tool to summarise it, with a quote and a clause number for each point.

Use the exhibit. The studio, the lease and the notes are made up for this case. Facts about the tools and policies are from the vendors' docs and the Anthropic Usage Policy, October 2026.
exhibit:
AI SUMMARY OF THE LEASE (made up)

  1. Rent: 4,200 a month, up 3% each year.
     Quote (4.2): "The Rent shall increase by
     three percent (3%) on each anniversary."
  2. Early exit: the studio may end the lease
     early at any time.
     Quote (9.1): "After the first twenty-four
     (24) months, the Tenant may terminate this
     Lease by giving six (6) months' written
     notice."
  3. Repairs: the landlord pays for all repairs.
     Quote: none given.

NOTES
  - Studio owner: "The summary looks complete.
    Can we sign tomorrow?"
  - A designer: "Can you run my own flat lease
    through the tool and tell me if I can break
    it?"

questions.prompt: Look at point 2 and its quote. What do you do?

options.text: Keep it, because the point comes with a real quote and a clause number
options.explanation: The quote is real, but the point says something the quote does not. Read the quote, not only the summary line.

options.text: Rewrite it from the quote: exit only after 24 months, with 6 months' notice
options.explanation: Right. The quote limits the exit in two ways that the summary line drops. The Claude docs suggest grounding answers in word-for-word quotes, so the quote wins over the summary.

options.text: Delete the quote from the summary, so the owner gets a shorter page
options.explanation: The quote is the part a person can check. Dropping it hides the mistake instead of fixing it.

options.text: Ask the tool to shorten the quote, so it matches the summary line
options.explanation: A shorter quote would lose the 24 months and the notice period. The summary must match the lease, not the other way round.

questions.prompt: Point 3 has no quote. What do you do with it?

options.text: Treat it as unsupported until someone finds the clause in the lease
options.explanation: Right. The Claude docs say to have each claim backed by a quote, and if no quote can be found, the claim must be taken back.

options.text: Keep it, since the other two points in the summary came with quotes
options.explanation: Each point stands on its own. A quote for point 1 says nothing about point 3.

options.text: Ask the tool "Are you sure?" and keep the point if the answer is yes
options.explanation: A yes from the same tool is not a quote from the lease. The check is the lease itself.

options.text: Change it to "the studio pays for all repairs" to be on the safe side
options.explanation: That swaps one unsupported claim for another. Nobody has read the repairs clause yet.

questions.prompt: The owner asks: "The summary looks complete. Can we sign tomorrow?" What do you answer?

options.text: Yes, because the tool quoted the lease, so nothing can be missing
options.explanation: Quotes show a point is in the lease. They do not show that nothing is missing. The Claude docs say these methods reduce hallucinations but don't remove them.

options.text: Yes, as long as a second AI tool gives the same summary of the lease
options.explanation: Two tools can miss the same thing. Matching summaries are not a legal review.

options.text: Yes, as long as the owner reads the summary twice before signing
options.explanation: Reading the summary again does not check what the summary left out, and the owner is not a lawyer.

options.text: Not yet: a lawyer reads the lease first, using the summary as a guide
options.explanation: Right. The ChatGPT docs say legal decisions need appropriate expert review. The summary can help the lawyer start faster.

questions.prompt: A designer asks you to run their own flat lease through the tool and say if they can break it. What do you do?

options.text: Run it and give them the answer, since it is only a small flat
options.explanation: Advice on a person's own legal rights is a high-risk use in the Anthropic Usage Policy, whatever the size of the flat.

options.text: Say no to any talk of leases, since every legal topic is banned
options.explanation: General explanations are allowed. The Anthropic Usage Policy excludes explaining what a law says without applying it to one person.

options.text: Say the tool can explain lease terms, but their own case needs a lawyer
options.explanation: Right. Advising a person on their own legal rights or on what to do in a specific legal matter is a high-risk use. A general explanation of terms is not.

options.text: Run it, and add a note that the studio is not responsible for it
options.explanation: A note does not make the advice safe. The designer may still act on it without a lawyer.
